correctness.rationale: The three-delay cosine orbit is an invertible linear image of a circle because sin(theta) is nonzero. Nearest-neighbour phase separation converges uniformly to zero on the irrational orbit. Exact chord identities reduce the future/three-delay ratio to r_theta at the chord midpoint, and the empirical absolute cutoff vanishes. Unique ergodicity converts the ratio test to a continuous angular quadratic-form event with finite, zero-measure boundary. The Gram determinant and generalized Rayleigh maximum yield E(z); two eigenvalues yield the exact arctangent fraction; direct differentiation and a degree-four irreducibility argument give the optimal irrational angle. CHECK.py passed exact symbolic identities and six finite-orbit approximations; numerical finite samples are not the proof.
